quote: und welches ist der Affekt der- selben, wenn man die Wurzeln von $f(x)=0$ [-...-] adjungirt?
english: and what is its affect (Galois group) when one adjoins the roots of f(x)=0?
topic: Three short notes: questions on the discriminant of a quadratic form built from the roots of an algebraic equation (the equation with real roots in lambda), a question on directly proving regularity of solutions of differential equations other than Laplace's, and the problem of counting the possible configurations of n circles in the plane.

triage.modern_statement: The question cannot be pinned down exactly. Our best reading: start from an algebraic equation f(x)=0, build a real quadratic form from its roots (possibly a Hermite/Sylvester-type form Σ(y0+α_i y1+…)^2), and take an associated equation in λ, for example det(Q−λE)=0. That equation has only real roots. Hilbert asks about its discriminant and about its Galois group ('Affekt') over the base field once the roots of f(x)=0 are adjoined. The excerpt has an illegible gap ('[-...-]') and does not say which form or which λ-equation is meant. So the exact object whose Galois group is asked for cannot be recovered.
triage.answered_by: No specific later answer found. The closest known literature is about the discriminant of a characteristic equation with only real roots: Kummer (1843) and Borchardt (1846) showed that the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of a real symmetric matrix is a sum of squares. Domokos refined this in 2010–2011 (arXiv:1003.0475). That work is about sum-of-squares representations, not about the Galois group Hilbert asks for.

evidence.claim: The discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of a real symmetric matrix (an equation in λ whose roots are all real) can be written as a sum of squares. The paper says this improves results of Kummer from 1843 and Borchardt from 1846. This is likely the classical setting of the page's first note.
The fact that this discriminant is a sum of squares goes back to Kummer and Borchardt and was later rediscovered and refined by several authors.
